**Performance: block** at `5de084c74c75ea63532bec6f4eb36a9f872092d7`.

Full review of the PR-owned commits against merge base `27efa69ced77776e3a25b990c68aa790c3f518bf`. Main's inherited changes are excluded. The new early refusal and client shutdown reduce work, but two attribution gaps prevent treating these counters as the complete instrument required by AC1/AC2.

## Findings

**P148-F001: a timed-out observer can launch ps after its tally was finalized.** `registration.rs:131-154` gives an attempt its own atomic read tally and samples it exactly once after registration returns. On macOS, `native_observer` at `1695-1718` runs the observation in `spawn_blocking`; the increment happens inside that worker immediately before `read_argv_with_ps`. The five-second timeouts at `325-381` and `453-465` can drop the awaiting future while its blocking worker remains queued or running. If the worker reaches the argv read afterward, the existing global `ps.registration-native-process` counter advances, but the attempt's previously recorded `ps`, `by_key` and `by_seat` never update. Its final atomic value is discarded. This loses attribution precisely on a loaded machine, where these timeout/retry paths matter.

Preserve attempt accounting until any surviving observer work finishes, or prevent queued timed-out work from launching after accounting closes. Add a deterministic test that holds an observer before its argv read, lets registration time out, then releases it and verifies that any paid read remains attributed to that attempt. This is a source-level finding, not a local reproduction. Linux CI does not compile the affected production observer branch.

**P148-F002: pre-service registration refusals are not counted.** `http/mod.rs:965-1007` returns before `register_via` for an invalid role, pane observation errors, a mismatched claimed process, or a disappeared pane. These are authenticated, parsed registration attempts, but `Path::from_client` and the counting wrapper only run afterward at `1010-1024`. Repeated failures there can therefore produce zero attempt deltas. AC1's "every attempt" claim needs an accounting boundary covering these outcomes too, without double-counting calls that reach the service. Include a valid-request/invalid-role refusal control in the ping contract test.

## Resource shape

| Surface | Cost and scaling |
|---|---|
| Attempt recording | One shared synchronous mutex, two BTreeMap tally updates, and seat-key allocation per completed service call. At most 180 enum combinations (10 paths x 2 modes x 9 outcomes), and 64 individually retained seat keys plus overflow. Registration also allocates an attempt atomic/Arc; the macOS observer owns its existing per-attempt ancestry cache. No new executable, timer, event or store write from counting. These are not atomics-only counters, despite the plan/backpressure wording. |
| Ping snapshot | Per explicit ping, the same mutex formats up to 180 keys, sums their totals, and clones at most 65 seat keys; serialization follows. Cost scales with retained key bytes as well as cardinality, not live seat count beyond the cap. |
| Early native refusal | One additional indexed seat lookup plus schema validation per explicit native address, including healthy claims. A different-session conflict returns before host observation; removing this early check leaves the same refusal under the registration lock, later. It is a brake, not a positive-proof cache. It avoids the existing ancestry reads/launches for that conflict class, not every tombstoned claim. |
| Existing observer | No new launch site. macOS retains absolute-path `/bin/ps`, at most once per host-named ancestor per attempt, with ancestry bounded to 32. Linux reads `/proc` in-process. Observer blocking tasks and bounded child observation already existed; the new tally adds an atomic increment at the argv-read boundary. |
| Heartbeat/re-attestation | One existing loop per native bridge. Healthy renewal waits the daemon's `renew_after_ms` (lease/3); failures back off from 250 ms to 5 s, with native-holder standby at 30 s or an earlier prompt. Only the typed HTTP-400 `/v1/register` retired refusal now holds receiving, aborts both controllers, reports once and ends the loop. This removes its indefinite retired re-registration traffic, formerly up to about 0.2 attempts/s per failed bridge after backoff, not counting request duration. |
| Receive/shim/binders | Receive's existing terminal-error path already holds both loops; the new typed retired diagnostic identifies that stop. Receive labels explicit/receive/standby retry; ordinary failures still recover. Shim per-call paneless preflight and Claude/Codex/adopt registration retain their previous cadence and work; this PR labels/counts them, not eliminates them. |

## Proof and remaining work

GitHub now reports this exact head CLEAN. [CI 42351634792](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42351634792) has all four jobs successful. Rust JUnit lists **2,027 executed cases, zero failures/errors**, including counter totals/overflow/unknown labels, service counting, ping exposure, the zero-observation retired refusal with a positive control, ancestry guards and all six spawn guards. Five Rust tests were skipped separately. Both Node jobs ran the new retired-discriminator and heartbeat-stop tests successfully; Node 22's native gate passed **323/323**, and generation-router passed **67/67**. [Delivers 42352055393](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42352055393) also succeeds. These tests do not cover either finding above.

AC2's live reading, AC5's near-zero at-rest goal, the healthy no-op repeat skip and shim per-call removal remain unproven/deferred, as the packet and unchecked tasks state. This is not completion of the plan's broader AC3/AC4 promises, nor a claim that issue #145 is fixed.

After the accounting fixes and an authorized deployment, capture two niced ping snapshots on the same verified daemon PID/build over an actual measured interval, after settling. Retain every registration `count`/`ps` delta by key and seat, the overflow bucket, and the global registration spawn delta. Reconcile both origins after in-flight observations settle; retain any mismatch rather than smoothing it. Rank the paths by paid ps/s, separately rank available seat attribution (the API does not cross-tabulate seat and path), and name overflow/older-client limitations. Pair the window with whole-machine launch rate and daemon CPU/RSS; do not subtract counters across PIDs. The earlier approximately 0.64 registration ps/s is a historical receipt, not a matched measurement of this head.

No local builds, tests, runtime probes, or review-worktree mutations were performed.
